item.title: Sepsis: when an infection turns deadly, and how to spot it early
item.description: Sepsis is linked to about one in five deaths worldwide, and the burden is highest in sub-Saharan Africa. What it is, the warning signs in adults and children, and why every hour counts.

item.title: Cough, cold or sore throat: when do you really need an antibiotic?
item.description: Most coughs, colds and sore throats get better without antibiotics. What the evidence says, which illnesses do need treatment, and the danger signs that mean you should go to a health facility now.

item.title: Why antibiotics are failing in Uganda, and what you can do about it
item.description: Antibiotic resistance is already making common infections harder to treat in Uganda. A plain-language guide to what it is, why it is happening here, and the simple things that help.
